reading: The input has objects of two colours. Each colour's objects are gathered into a column (the colour that sits further left in the input goes left at column 0; the other starts after a one-column gap). In each column the objects are left-aligned and stacked upward from the bottom row, with one empty row between slots.
verb: sort into colour columns and stack

slots.subject: every object (8-connected, one colour)
slots.column: one column per colour, left colour first, left edges at 0 and at left-width+1
slots.order: objects stacked bottom-up in shared row slots with a one-row gap; the order within a column is not settled from the training pairs

why: every input object appears exactly once in the output with the same shape, grouped by colour and resting on the bottom

reading: The 3x3 panels each hold one piece of a pattern, placed off-centre inside the panel. Each panel's content moves to the panel whose position in the 3x3 layout matches where the piece sits inside its own panel (a top-left piece goes to the top-left panel). The full pattern goes to the centre panel.

slots.unit: the 9 panels cut by the background separator lines
slots.key: the position of the non-majority cells inside each panel (corner, edge, or whole)
slots.target: the panel at that same position in the 3x3 panel layout

why: the output panels are a permutation of the input panels, and each lands at the slot that matches where its piece lies inside the panel

reading: Each panel (cut by the full separator lines) holds four 3x3 blocks. If the panel has a colour-4 axis line, the two halves on either side of it swap places (a mirror across the 4 line). Otherwise every colour-1 placeholder block takes the panel's single other block colour.
verb: per panel: swap across the axis or fill placeholders

slots.unit: each panel between the separator lines
slots.case_axis: a 4-line inside the panel: mirror the blocks across it
slots.case_no_axis: recolour the 1-blocks to the panel's other block colour

why: panels with a 4 line come out mirrored across it; panels without one come out with all blocks one colour

reading: The grid is a woven lattice of row types and column types. A few cells are marked 8. Every other place where the exact same local neighbourhood appears (in either orientation, rows and columns swapped) gets its matching cells recoloured to 8.

slots.template: the 8-cells together with the lattice context around them
slots.match: every location (incl. transposed) whose surrounding cells equal the template's context

why: every new 8 sits at a spot whose neighbourhood is identical to an original 8-spot's neighbourhood; nothing else changes

reading: Some rows contain a 1 and, further right, an 8. For each such row, take the cells strictly between the 1 and the 8. Stack these runs top to bottom to form the output.

slots.rows: rows holding both a 1 and an 8
slots.segment: the cells strictly between the 1 and the 8
slots.assemble: stack the segments in row order

why: every output row is exactly the stretch between the 1 and the 8 on one input row; the stretches have equal length

reading: There are partial plus/cross shapes drawn in 2 on a noisy 5 background. Each cross is completed to a symmetric plus (equal arms, length 2 or 3 as the visible 2s show), and the missing cells of the plus become 8.

slots.subject: each partial plus of 2s (centre and four arms)
slots.region: the plus cells that are not 2

why: after the change each cross is a full symmetric plus of 2 and 8; only cells on those pluses change

reading: Each colour-6 shape takes the colour of the single marker cell nearest to it. The shapes are then cropped to their boxes and joined side by side (left to right, or top to bottom when they are stacked vertically).
verb: recolour by nearest marker and concatenate

slots.subject: the 6-coloured shapes
slots.assemble: concatenate the shapes' bounding boxes along the axis they are spread along, in order

why: the output is the shapes' boxes placed next to each other, each recoloured to its marker's colour

reading: A diagonal (up-right) line of 2s is replaced by a line one cell longer that continues on the same anti-diagonal, starting right after the old line's upper end. The old line is erased.

slots.subject: the diagonal segment of 2s, length n
slots.target: the next n+1 cells further up-right on the same anti-diagonal

why: the output segment lies on the same anti-diagonal, touches the old segment's end, and has length n+1

reading: One small shape of 8 shows a template. Every group of 3-cells that forms the same shape (rotations allowed) is recoloured to 8.
verb: recolour copies of the template shape

slots.template: the shape formed by the 8 cells
slots.subject: 3-coloured groups whose shape equals the template up to rotation

why: every changed cell was 3 and belongs to a copy of the 8-template; nothing else changes

reading: One shape has a single 8 cell embedded in it. Crop that shape's 3x3 box, then repaint the 8 cell in the shape's own colour.
why: the output is the box of the multi-coloured component, with the 8 cell replaced by the colour around it
invariants: shape outline of the chosen object
